subject: Clarify: where requests are executed + deletion schedule (ClarityRx)
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@clarityrx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Park <tom.park@clarityrx.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick Q on processing loci and delete commitments

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. The engineering and security teams here at ClarityRx had a few targeted follow-ups before we move to procurement: specifically we need a concise answer on (1) where our inference payloads would be executed (region/hops/subprocessors) if we use Redwood's hosted API, and (2) the deletion / backup retention timeline for customer content and logs.

A couple of concrete asks to help our security checklist:
- A one-page map of geographic execution points for requests originating in the US East coast and APAC.
- Names of any subprocessors that see payloads (inference/runtime, logging, backups).
- Exact SLA for deletion after a customer-initiated erase (soft delete vs permanent removal).

We need to include this in our vendor risk assessment this week. Can you send something we can attach?

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Security & Privacy Lead, ClarityRx

---
Note: we'd prefer a short summary we can share with legal (bullet points) and then a link to any evidence artifacts (SOC2, subprocessor list).
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@clarityrx.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q on processing loci and delete commitments

Elena —

Thanks for the clear ask. Quick summary up front, then attachments and evidence links below. If helpful I can schedule a 30-minute handoff with Jordan (network/ops) and Ben (product/security).

Short answers (bullet summary you can paste into your assessment):
- Where requests execute: Primary execution occurs in the region you select at API time; for US-based customers we default to US-west (Oregon) or US-east (Ashburn) depending on routing policy. We also maintain execution POPs in EU (Frankfurt) and APAC (Singapore) for regional customers.
- Cross-border behavior: For hosted API, request data may transit to a nearby POP for lower latency; persistent processing (model state, logs) is stored only in the configured region except for encrypted backups which replicate to a secondary region for disaster recovery unless you request region-pin.
- Subprocessors: runtime GPU hosts (GigaCloud Operations), object storage (FastStore Inc.), and a logging pipeline (LogStream). Full CSV attached.
- Deletion SLA: soft-delete (logical erase) occurs immediately on API erase request; primary storage scrub completes within 30 days; backups are rotated and purged on a 90-day schedule; residual snapshots in cold archives are purged within 180 days. We provide a deletion certificate once the process completes.

Attachments: Redwood_Processing_Locations_v1.pdf (map + short explanations), subprocessor_inventory_20270425.csv, SOC2-Type2-Redwood-redacted.pdf (summary).

If you need stricter guarantees (e.g., no cross-region replication, on-prem/private deployment), we can propose Redwood Private with region-pin and no offsite backups.

Next step options:
1) Accept this evidence and proceed to the SOX/security questionnaire step.
2) Book a 30-minute technical call to review the execution map.

Which do you prefer?

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Marissa —

Appreciate the quick summary. A couple follow-ups from our infra team:
- Can you confirm whether the encrypted backups that replicate to a secondary region are accessible by Redwood engineers or only by your KMS/HSM?
- For the 30-day primary scrub, does that include inference-specific KV cache evictions (i.e., any persisted prefix caches or only persisted logs)?

Also — Elena asked if you can provide a short (one-paragraph) explanation we can insert verbatim into our vendor memo describing how Redwood routes requests when the customer chooses the hosted API.

On a logistics note, we need SOC2 evidence (redacted ok) and a copy of the most recent subprocessor inventory; would be great if you can drop these into the Drive folder (link below) so our procurement can pull them into the packet.

Thanks,
Tom Park
Director, Infrastructure — ClarityRx

Tom / Elena —

Answers inline and evidence uploaded to the Drive link you provided. Docs uploaded: SOC2 redacted, subprocessor CSV, and a 1-page execution map PDF.

- Backup access: Backups are encrypted with customer-tenant keys managed in Redwood's KMS; Redwood SREs do not have KMS plaintext access unless an out-of-band emergency procedure is initiated (audited, requires supervisor approval, and recorded in an access log). If you need HSM-backed keys under your tenancy, we support that via the Private deployment.

- KV cache / persisted caches: Transient KV caches used for in-flight request acceleration are not written to persistent storage by default. If your integration uses explicit cache pins (customers can opt-in for cache persistence for performance), those pins are stored in the customer region and are subject to the same deletion SLA. We will confirm with Jordan if any cached artifacts for your suggested prompts would be persisted by default.

- One-paragraph routing blurb you can paste verbatim:
Redwood routes API requests to the nearest available execution POP based on customer routing policy and latency. For hosted customers the request may transit regional POPs for performance and failover; persistent artifacts (models, logs, customer-managed caches) are stored only in the configured primary region unless replication is enabled for disaster recovery.

Next steps: Jordan will follow up with a short check (15 minutes) to confirm cache behavior for your workload and Ben will provide the redaction guidance on the SOC2. If that's OK, I'll mark this as "evidence provided" in our deal and share the HubSpot record with procurement.

Thanks —
Marissa

--
